correctness.rationale: For every circuit-hyperplane H, new-basis neighbors form the full rank-by-corank rook graph; its flag link has a row/column simplex cover with nerve K_{r,s} of first Betti (r-1)(s-1). The new star attaches along this link, and simple connectivity of K(M) makes the map of its circle wedge null-homotopic, so the homotopy cofiber splits. In the Fano case, exact exhaustive checker confirms every simplex/face incidence, acyclicity of 154 pairs on 322 cells leaving 1 zero-cell and 13 two-cells, and independently 182 pairs on 384 relaxed cells leaving 1 zero-cell and 19 two-cells. The finite certificates are proof under Forman theory, not extrapolation from experiments. General conclusion is explicitly conditional.

value.rationale: The Fano versus non-Fano pair is the canonical binary/nonbinary circuit-hyperplane relaxation and a natural test of exchange-network topology. Their flag complex homotopy ranks differ by precisely six, and the structural (r-1)(n-r-1) splitting applies to arbitrary matroid relaxations satisfying a topologically checkable condition. This transfers homotopy information through a fundamental matroid operation rather than recomputing an arbitrary small graph count; prior triangle-square results cannot supply these flag invariants.
